content.title: Video by linusoyugi
content.description:
Feminism didn’t primarily liberate the average woman.
It primarily enriched a tiny minority of men.
Expanding women’s paid work increased the labor supply.
That put downward pressure on wages and weakened workers’ bargaining power.
The biggest winners? Capitalists — mostly men — who got a larger, cheaper workforce.
Sex-positivity messaging framed casual sex as empowerment.
It increased the supply of short-term sex.
Men (on average higher in sociosexuality) benefit far more from this than women do.
The orgasm gap in casual sex makes that clear: men 80–90%, women 30–40%.
So the real beneficiaries of modern feminism aren’t most women.
They’re a small group of already-powerful or highly promiscuous men.
Technology and individual-rights ideas did the heavy lifting for women’s actual freedom.
Feminism just handed extra advantages to the few at the top.

#Feminism
#GenderDebate
#SexPositivity
#CasualSex
#orgasmgap

transcription.full_text: I would like to understand why, again, you think that men benefit from feminism more? I wouldn't really argue that men in general have benefited from feminism more than women. I would argue that a tiny minority of people who happen to be mostly men have benefited from feminism more than women. And they are capitalists and dark-tetrid men. While I'm in total agreement with feminists that women have indeed faced many historical injustices throughout history, where I tend to disagree with them is the true reason why women are much freer today. I don't think traditional feminism alone deserves the credit. I strongly believe that technology and the exchange of ideas between cultures were the primary drivers. Technologies like the washing machine, the dishwasher and reliable bath control reduced domestic burden and gave women better control, making careers and education far more accessible. And at the same time, as societies interacted, harmful practices such as female genital mutilation and child marriage increasingly came under challenge from ideas centered on individual freedom and human rights. Let me now explain to you how feminism benefits men more than it does women. Expanding paid employment of women increased labor supply, which all else equal exerts a downward pressure on wages. And capitalists, who are mostly men, benefited from a larger pool of workers, a higher labor force participation, and weakened bargaining power of the existing workforce. In other words, feminism made the rich, who are mostly men, even more richer. And secondly, sex positivity messaging, which frames casual sex as liberating for women, increases the supply of short-term mating opportunities. This disproportionately benefits men who tend to score higher in what we call sociosexuality, in other words, willingness to participate in non-committal sex. The average woman, as we know, is less oriented toward and less psychologically rewarded by casual sex. This is indicated by the fact that women report substantially lower rates of orgasm in casual sex compared to men. Men report 80 to 90 percent rates of orgasm in casual sex compared to women 30 to 40 percent.

content_analysis.primary_theme: A creator argues that feminism's material gains were captured by capitalists and high-sociosexuality men rather than by women, and that technology rather than feminism drove women's freedom.
secondary_themes: Labour-supply mechanism: expanded female employment raised labour supply and weakened the bargaining power of the existing workforce
Technological rather than ideological causation — washing machine, dishwasher, reliable birth control
Cross-cultural exchange credited with challenging FGM and child marriage
Sociosexuality asymmetry, supported by an orgasm-rate statistic in casual sex
content_analysis.rhetorical_frame: Concession then redirection. He grants historical injustice against women, then reassigns credit for their liberation and reassigns the beneficiary of the movement.
notable_speakers: An unheard interlocutor whose question opens the clip

key_moments.note: Names the beneficiary class directly: 'they are capitalists and dark-tetrad men'
Credits technology and cross-cultural exchange over feminism for women's freedom
The labour-supply argument: more workers, higher participation, weakened bargaining power, 'feminism made the rich, who are mostly men, even more richer'
Sex-positivity argument and the orgasm-rate statistic (80–90% men vs 30–40% women in casual sex), stated without citation

framework_notes.extraction_kernel: Named explicitly, which is rare in this corpus. He identifies capital as the party that captured the gains: expanded labour supply, higher participation, weakened bargaining power of the existing workforce, and 'feminism made the rich even more richer'. That is a structurally sound account of surplus capture — an increase in labour supply against fixed demand does transfer bargaining power from labour to capital.
framework_notes.buffer_class: Left unnamed, and its absence drives the argument's conclusion. He describes a transfer from labour to capital, which is a vertical movement, then addresses the grievance to feminism and to women rather than to the party he just identified as the beneficiary.
framework_notes.psychological_wage: The sociosexuality section trades in status rather than material terms. The orgasm-rate asymmetry is offered as evidence of who benefits, converting a material argument about wages into a status argument about sexual access. No source is given for the figures.
framework_notes.snubber_circuits: None operating in this clip. The argument runs toward confrontation with feminism rather than dissipating pressure.
framework_notes.electrodynamic_map: He resolves $\vec{E}$ correctly and then applies the force along the wrong axis. The material field is real and he locates it — capital capturing the surplus of an expanded labour pool. The prescription that follows travels along $\vec{v} \times \vec{B}$, landing on gender, so the identified vertical mechanism produces horizontal motion. An accurate reading of the extraction kernel arrives at a grievance addressed to fellow labour.
framework_notes.thermodynamic_map: Work is genuinely described here: a real transfer of material value from wage-earners to capital owners. The reel's own output, at 174 likes and 12 comments, is small — this is a low-current node relative to the second reel in this batch, despite carrying the more mechanically accurate account.
framework_notes.systems_dynamics: A correct sensor feeding a misrouted actuator. The measurement stage identifies capital; the response stage targets feminism. In control terms the feedback loop stabilises the extraction kernel it has just described, because the corrective energy is directed at a party with no control over the field.
framework_notes.evidence_limits: The orgasm-rate figures and the labour-supply claim are asserted without citation and are not verified here. Whether he elsewhere directs any argument at capital is unknown from this clip alone; the framework reading describes the structure of this 131 seconds and makes no claim about his broader position. OCR produced no usable rows, so no on-screen text supports or qualifies the speech.

widgets.caption: He names this flow himself: more workers entering paid employment transfers bargaining power, and therefore material value, from labour to capital. This is the first reel in the corpus to identify an extraction kernel explicitly.

Unusually, the material field is not near zero — he describes a real transfer. The deflection happens anyway: the grievance is addressed along the gender axis rather than at the capital he identified.
